questions.q: What is df.merge(other, on="col", how="left") the pandas equivalent of?
options: Sorting a DataFrame by that column
Dropping duplicate rows
A SQL LEFT JOIN on that shared column
A SQL DELETE statement
questions.explain: merge() combines two DataFrames on a shared key, the same way a SQL join combines two tables.

questions.q: In the priority-table example, why did 4 rows end up with ship_priority as NaN after a how="left" merge?
options: Those 4 rows all belong to the Accessories category, which was missing from the priority reference table
NaN appears randomly and has no connection to the merge key
left merges always produce some NaN values regardless of the data
Those rows had missing customer_name values
questions.explain: The priority DataFrame only listed Footwear, Camping, and Packs — Accessories had no match, so its rows got NaN instead of being dropped.

questions.q: What happened to the same 4 Accessories rows when the merge used how="inner" instead of how="left"?
options: Nothing changed — inner and left always produce identical results
They were dropped entirely, since inner only keeps rows that match on both sides
They were kept with ship_priority set to "Standard"
They were duplicated
questions.explain: how="inner" keeps only rows with a match in both DataFrames, dropping the result from 20 rows to 16.

questions.q: Why is a NaN appearing after a left merge actually useful, rather than just a problem to hide?
options: NaN values always indicate a bug in pandas itself
NaN values should always be immediately deleted from the DataFrame
It's a visible signal that the merge key had no match on the other side for that row, which an inner merge would have hidden by silently dropping the row
It means the merge failed completely and must be re-run
questions.explain: An inner merge gives no such warning sign — rows that don't match just disappear, which is easy to miss if you only check len(result).

questions.q: In this lesson's warehouses example, how many rows does orders.csv end up with after merging with the warehouses DataFrame on "region" using how="left"?
options: 20 — every region in orders.csv has a matching warehouse
0 — the merge fails
4 — one per region
16 — some orders have no matching region
questions.explain: All four regions (West, East, South, North) exist in the warehouses table, so no rows are lost and none get NaN.
